requirements.requirement: Run node1 in AS 65100 as the BGP transit router between node2/AS 65101 and node3/AS 65102.
requirements.summary: Final post-restart observations show established node1 sessions to 172.20.1.1 in AS 65101 and 172.20.2.1 in AS 65102, with reciprocal peer sessions to AS 65100. Node1's reboot transition and boot-identity cross-check are complete.

requirements.requirement: Use peer-a and peer-b for BGP and endpoint transit while keeping the management network outside that data path.
requirements.summary: The peer /31s are on node1 eth1/eth2 and Ubuntu enp8s0, while management addresses and default routes remain on node1 eth0 and Ubuntu enp1s0. Final route lookups and node1 captures place endpoint traffic on the dedicated interfaces.

requirements.requirement: Give each Ubuntu peer a stable endpoint prefix and have it originate only its own prefix.
requirements.summary: After peer restarts, node2 retains 198.51.100.2/32 and exactly that BGP network statement; node3 retains 203.0.113.3/32 and exactly that statement. Node1 receives one prefix from each peer. Both restart protocols include healthy baselines, acknowledgements, changed boot IDs, and recovered networking, BGP, routes, and transit; lifecycle boot IDs agree.

requirements.requirement: Have node1 learn both endpoint routes and provide bidirectional transit without changing endpoint source addresses.
requirements.summary: Node1 has best installed routes through eth1 and eth2; each peer installs the remote endpoint with an AS path through 65100. Final source-bound pings succeed in both directions, and captures on both node1 interfaces show identical endpoint source and destination addresses across transit.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final and post-restart evidence. The required AS topology, dedicated-link routing, stable single-prefix origination, learned transit routes, bidirectional forwarding, and packet-level source preservation are demonstrated. The separate provider restart protocol is complete and independently corroborated for all three nodes. Hygiene is reduced by two retained unrelated or redundant configuration changes, a corrected systemd-cycle attempt, a transient failed apply restart, and two leftover capture logs.
limitations: No explicit advertised-routes dump was captured from the Ubuntu peers; exclusive origination is established by their final single network statements and node1 receiving exactly one prefix from each.

Lifecycle collection is bounded and does not inventory all persistent configuration files. The initial node1 discovery output is also truncated, so exact baseline comparison for docker0 and retained CONFIG_DB state relies partly on the complete executor command trace.

The node1 listening-socket delta after the mandatory reboot includes standard SONiC processes not explicitly enabled by any executor command; causal attribution is indeterminate, so those listeners were not treated as executor-created exposure.

operational_hygiene.summary: Restart evidence is complete on all nodes, package checks remain healthy, and node1's failed units were already present before execution. Deductions: cmd-7b130b4e89184c34 embedded unrelated docker0 address removal and forced shutdown in the enabled startup path, which remained enabled after reboot. cmd-ad29093596af4435 persisted neighbor keys that did not instantiate after the BGP restart in cmd-bf9a8078d93b4a97; recovery still lacked those peers in cmd-ef6b59bd105c41c8, and the working custom peer service was subsequently created by cmd-f11b42d9e672407f. No removal of that redundant CONFIG_DB state is captured; the restart experiment itself was transient and recovered. The custom units were initially attached to sonic.target by cmd-7b130b4e89184c34 and cmd-f11b42d9e672407f, producing the cycle observed in cmd-d66840a12e9d47ef; cmd-5f67850efc594682 fully corrected this before reboot. Finally, cmd-720ec9e2e8f34970 left two tcpdump evidence logs in /tmp, confirmed by the final lifecycle snapshot.
